tierReasoning: Roughly 50 lines across two source files: one new exported loader with a two-step resolution order, and one injectable seam passing a path the orchestrator already holds. No new capability, no route, no config key, no migration, no irreversibility; the classifier's rules are byte-identical and the fail-closed catch-all is unchanged and now asserted. It does touch src/localVerify/**, the merge authority's own server side, so if the gate's risk floor signals higher the override is deliberate: the compensating rigour is a full ELI16, a full eight-question side-effects artifact, a measured fail-first proof, and three rounds of independent second-pass review that caught two real overstatements and two defects in my own test file.

causalAutopsy.notes: Latent since skipRatchet.ts shipped. Its own doc comment stated the assumption that made it wrong: 'typescript is a devDependency of instar; it is present wherever a source checkout exists (local-verify is repo-gated)'. That is true of the CHECKOUT and false of the PROCESS: the verifier is loaded from the agent's shadow install, a production npm install carrying no devDependencies. The assumption was never tested because the unit tests run inside a source checkout, where the module's own require succeeds — a blind instrument, not a missing test. Surfaced only when PR 2318 was held overnight on an unexplained harness flag and the run log (not the service audit log, where I first looked) named the cause. Class lesson: any module the SERVER loads from the shadow install may require runtime dependencies only; a devDependency require there fails in production and is invisible in development.
